title: Acute Pulmonary Hypertension Decompensation and Right-Heart Failure

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with acute right ventricular (RV) failure, including acute decompensation of known pulmonary hypertension (PH), in the emergency department (ED), coronary care or intensive care unit (ICU): recognition, severity assessment, treatment of the trigger, fluid and diuretic strategy, vasopressor and inotrope support, ventilation cautions and referral to a PH centre. Uses the Heart Failure Association and European Society of Cardiology (HFA/ESC) 2016 statement on acute RV failure, the Saudi Association for Pulmonary Hypertension 2014 guideline and US product labels. Acute pulmonary embolism and RV infarction have their own topics; their specific reperfusion treatment is not repeated here.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-21.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The 2022 ESC/European Respiratory Society PH guideline could not be opened; the Saudi 2014 guideline and the HFA/ESC 2016 statement are used.
The HFA/ESC 2016 document is a consensus statement, not a graded guideline.
Levosimendan and phosphodiesterase III inhibitors are named by HFA/ESC 2016 but their labels were not opened, so they are not listed as regimens.

Epoprostenol for decompensated New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class IV pulmonary arterial hypertension is started in a PH centre; only the Saudi 2014 starting dose is quoted and the label was not opened.
Typical adult normal ranges for lactate, natriuretic peptides, troponin, liver and renal tests are not from these sources; local laboratory ranges apply.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Acute RV failure is a rapidly progressive syndrome of systemic congestion from impaired RV filling and/or reduced RV output (HFA/ESC 2016, Introduction). Pressure or volume overload dilates the RV and worsens tricuspid regurgitation, raising venous pressure (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 1). A dilated RV shifts the septum left and increases pericardial constraint, underfilling the left ventricle and causing low output and shock (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 2). Venous congestion impairs kidney, gut and liver function, which predicts poor prognosis (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Consequences of right ventricular failure). Hypoxia, hypercapnia, acidosis and hypothermia cause pulmonary vasoconstriction and raise RV afterload (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).

symptoms: Abdominal swelling and leg oedema from congestion (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 2).
Syncope in advanced PH with right heart failure (Saudi PH 2014, Section Modified NYHA functional class IV).
physicalSigns: Jugular venous distension and hepatojugular reflux (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 2).
Third heart sound and tricuspid regurgitation murmur (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 2).
Low output: hypotension, tachycardia, cool peripheries, confusion, oliguria (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 2).
redFlags: Hypotension, cool peripheries, oliguria or rising lactate: low-output state needing ICU-level monitoring (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 2 and Figure 4).
Suspected pulmonary embolism or RV infarction: prioritise cause-specific reperfusion (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 2).
Pericardial tamponade can mimic RV failure; exclude with echocardiography (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Echocardiographic assessment).
Intubation and positive pressure ventilation raise RV afterload and sedation can cause collapse (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
precipitants: Infection and sepsis, the most frequent trigger in pulmonary arterial hypertension (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
Anaemia and iron deficiency (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
Non-adherence to or withdrawal of PH treatment (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
Acute pulmonary embolism, left heart failure, RV ischaemia, lung disease exacerbation (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Thrombi in proximal pulmonary arteries, McConnell sign, tricuspid jet 2.8 to 3.5 m/s (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 3).
RV hypertrophy, tricuspid jet often above 3.5 m/s, right atrial enlargement (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 3).
Pericardial effusion with right atrial and RV diastolic collapse (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 3).
RV dilation and hypokinesia with normal or slightly raised pulmonary pressure (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 3).

differentials.condition: Left heart failure with secondary PH (group 2)
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Features of left heart disease dominate (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension; Saudi PH 2014, Section Group II).

ruleIn.modalityTarget: RV size, function and load; exclude tamponade
ruleIn.expectedFinding: RV dilation, septal shift, reduced tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), raised tricuspid jet velocity
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: First-line test in ED or ICU; estimates right atrial pressure from inferior vena cava size (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Echocardiographic assessment).
ruleIn.normalValue: RV smaller than left ventricle; TAPSE above 1.7 cm; tricuspid jet below 2.8 m/s (typical adult values)

clinicalManagement.title: Assess severity and place of care
actions: Assess blood pressure, mental state and urine output; send lactate, renal and liver tests, BNP and troponin; do bedside echocardiography (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 1).
Admit unstable patients to ICU or intermediate care with haemodynamic monitoring (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 6).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat the trigger
actions: Treat sepsis, arrhythmia and treatment withdrawal; reperfuse pulmonary embolism or RV infarction (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 2).
Keep arterial oxygen saturation above 90% (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
Restart or continue the patient's PH-specific treatment with the PH team (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).

clinicalManagement.title: Optimise fluid
actions: Congestion with maintained blood pressure: give intravenous loop diuretic (see Medicines) (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Volume optimization and Table 4).
Low blood pressure with low central venous pressure: cautious fluid, more than 200 mL over 15 to 30 minutes; avoid overfilling (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4).
Renal replacement therapy if diuretics fail (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 3).

clinicalManagement.title: Support blood pressure and output
actions: Restore blood pressure with noradrenaline (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 4).
Add an inotrope such as dobutamine to improve output; combine with noradrenaline if blood pressure falls (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Vasopressor and inotrope treatment).

clinicalManagement.title: Avoid harmful ventilation
actions: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) may help hypercapnic respiratory failure that does not respond to general measures (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
Avoid intubation and positive pressure ventilation where possible; if unavoidable, involve senior anaesthesia and ICU (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).

clinicalManagement.title: Specialist escalation
actions: Decompensated class IV pulmonary arterial hypertension: continuous intravenous epoprostenol is first line in a PH centre, starting dose 2 ng/kg/min (Saudi PH 2014, Section Modified NYHA functional class IV; class I).
Refractory cases: discuss mechanical support, atrial septostomy or lung transplant at an expert centre (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 6; Saudi PH 2014, Section Modified NYHA functional class IV).

regimens.indication: Venous congestion in acute RV failure
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with congestion and maintained blood pressure
regimens.dose: Not on oral diuretics: 20 to 40 mg intravenously; on chronic diuretics: at least the equivalent of the oral dose (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4). Inject slowly over 1 to 2 minutes; may repeat or raise by 20 mg no sooner than 2 hours after the previous dose (Furosemide label, Section Dosage and Administration).
adjustments: May worsen renal function and cause hypokalaemia (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4).
Resistant oedema: adding a thiazide-type diuretic or spironolactone may be considered (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Urine output, weight, renal function and potassium (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4).
Fluid status by echocardiography (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Pulmonary hypertension).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to furosemide (Furosemide label, Section Contraindications).

regimens.patientGroup: Adults with acute RV failure and hypotension
regimens.dose: 0.2 to 1.0 µg/kg/min (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4); label: start 8 to 12 µg/min, adjust to response, typical maintenance 2 to 4 µg/min (Norepinephrine label, Section 2.2).
regimens.route: Continuous intravenous infusion into a large vein
regimens.duration: Until blood pressure is stable; wean gradually
adjustments: Reduce gradually; abrupt stop causes marked hypotension (Norepinephrine label, Section 5.2).
Excessive vasoconstriction may worsen tissue perfusion (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure every 2 minutes until stable, then every 5 minutes (Norepinephrine label, Section 2.2).
Rhythm: may cause arrhythmia (Norepinephrine label, Section 5.3).
Infusion site for extravasation (Norepinephrine label, Section 5.1).
contraindications: No contraindications in the label (Norepinephrine label, Section 4).
Contains sodium metabisulfite; sulfite allergy (Norepinephrine label, Section 5.4).

regimens.indication: Low cardiac output in acute RV failure
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with acute RV failure and low output
regimens.dose: 2 to 20 µg/kg/min (HFA/ESC 2016, Table 4); start low at 0.5 to 1 µg/kg/min and titrate every few minutes (Dobutamine label, Section Dosage and Administration).
adjustments: May lower blood pressure; add noradrenaline if so (HFA/ESC 2016, Section Vasopressor and inotrope treatment).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure, heart rate, ectopy and urine output during titration (Dobutamine label, Section Dosage and Administration).
contraindications: Idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis (Dobutamine label, Section Contraindications).
Previous hypersensitivity to dobutamine or any component; contains sulfite (Dobutamine label, Sections Contraindications and Warnings).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Rapidly progressive systemic congestion from impaired RV filling and/or reduced RV output (HFA/ESC 2016, Introduction).
Blood pressure, mental state, urine output, lactate, liver and renal markers, natriuretic peptide, troponin and echocardiography (HFA/ESC 2016, Figure 4 Step 1).
Echocardiography screens; right heart catheterisation confirms (Saudi PH 2014, Section Echocardiography; class I).

teaching.scope: Adults with acute right ventricular (RV) failure, including acute decompensation of known pulmonary hypertension (PH), in the emergency department (ED), coronary care or intensive care unit (ICU): recognition, severity assessment, treatment of the trigger, fluid and diuretic strategy, vasopressor and inotrope support, ventilation cautions and referral to a PH centre. Uses the Heart Failure Association and European Society of Cardiology (HFA/ESC) 2016 statement on acute RV failure, the Saudi Association for Pulmonary Hypertension 2014 guideline and US product labels. Acute pulmonary embolism and RV infarction have their own topics; their specific reperfusion treatment is not repeated here.
learningObjectives: Recognise acute RV failure and its low-output state.
Use diuretics for congestion and cautious fluid only when filling pressure is low.
Support pressure with noradrenaline and output with an inotrope.
pitfalls: Giving fluid boluses to a congested, dilated RV.
Using dobutamine alone in a hypotensive patient.
keyPoints: Infection is the most common trigger in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Most patients need diuresis, not fluid.

patientEducation: Your right heart is struggling against high lung pressures; infection or missed medicines can trigger this.
Never stop PH medicines without your specialist.
Weigh yourself daily and report gains or swelling.
lifestyleAndDiet: Fluid and salt advice as set by the PH or heart failure team.
Rehabilitation programme once stable (Saudi PH 2014, Section Modified NYHA functional class IV; class I).
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; cardiologist or PH specialist; intensivist; echocardiography service; PH centre for prostanoid therapy, mechanical support or transplant referral (HFA/ESC 2016, Section General overview; Saudi PH 2014).
dischargeCriteria: Off vasoactive drugs, congestion improved, renal function stable, trigger treated, PH treatment plan confirmed by PH centre, follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: PH centre review with functional class and echocardiography; urgent lung transplant evaluation for class IV (Saudi PH 2014, Section Modified NYHA functional class IV).
